name: Finding the sweet spot in model tuning
gist: Modern large models need fine-tuning to new tasks, but this is expensive. Papers ask: how can you adapt models with fewer computations and memory without losing quality?
explain: You have a large language model trained on general text, but you need it to work on medical documents or to follow your company's style. Retraining from scratch on your data costs millions of dollars and takes weeks. So instead you do fine-tuning: you take the pretrained model and retrain it on your specific data, but you use a tiny learning rate so the base knowledge stays intact while the top layers adapt. The problem is that even fine-tuning is expensive—you still need to store and update millions of numbers for every example, and memory fills up quickly.

The challenge is to squeeze quality out of fewer computations and less memory. If you only update a few of the numbers inside the model, training is fast but the model does not adapt well. If you update everything, quality is good but you run out of memory. If you want both—fast adaptation and quality results—you need to be selective: identify which parts of the model matter most, or find a clever way to represent changes so you store less data. You also need to know when to stop: train too little and the model is useless, train too much and it forgets what it learned before.

Papers tackle this with methods like low-rank updates (store the change to the model as a product of two small matrices instead of one big one, saving memory), adapter modules (plug small trainable layers into the model and leave the base untouched), and pruning (identify which numbers in the model matter and update only those). Others study the math of learning rates and stopping times: at what point do the model's predictions stop improving? Some papers combine fine-tuning with distillation—train a smaller student model that mimics the large model's predictions, so you deploy something fast. The insight is that small targeted changes can adapt a model as well as retraining everything, if you pick the right targets.

papers.title: CompleteP for RL: Maintaining Feature Learning When Scaling Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Shows agents trained with CompleteP significantly improve compute and reward efficiency compared to NTK parameterization across control tasks.

papers.title: CurvZO: Adaptive Curvature-Guided Sparse Zeroth-Order Optimization for Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Improves fine-tuning accuracy by up to 4.4 points and achieves 2x speedup while preserving memory efficiency across OPT and Llama models on diverse NLP tasks.

papers.title: Explainable Token-level Noise Filtering for LLM Fine-tuning Datasets
papers.contribution: Improves downstream performance by up to 13.7% on math, code, and medicine tasks across 7 mainstream LLMs, highlighting importance of token-level optimization.

papers.title: Generalizable Heuristic Generation Through LLMs with Meta-Optimization
papers.contribution: MoH constructs effective and interpretable meta-optimizers achieving state-of-the-art performance on various combinatorial optimization problems, particularly in cross-size generalization settings.

papers.title: HiFo-Prompt: Prompting with Hindsight and Foresight for LLM-based Automatic Heuristic Design
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art automated heuristic design methods with higher-quality heuristics and substantially improved convergence speed.

papers.title: Hyperparameter Transfer with Mixture-of-Expert Layers
papers.contribution: Reliable hyperparameter transfer demonstrated across models from 51M to 2B parameters; small-model HPs transferred to large models on longer training horizons show performant behavior.

papers.title: Refining Hybrid Genetic Search for CVRP via Reinforcement Learning-Finetuned LLM
papers.contribution: Fine-tuned LLM generates crossover operators exceeding expert designs and outperforming GPT-4o on CVRP instances up to 1000 nodes.

papers.title: Seesaw: Accelerating Training by Balancing Batch Size and Learning Rate Scheduling
papers.contribution: Matches cosine decay at equal FLOPs while reducing wall-clock time by ~36% on 150M-600M models, approaching theoretical limits.

papers.title: $\alpha$-PFN: Fast Entropy Search via In-Context Learning
papers.contribution: Competitive with state-of-the-art entropy search on benchmarks while achieving over 50x speedups.

papers.title: $\mu$pscaling small models: Principled warm starts and hyperparameter transfer
papers.contribution: Proves upscaled models are functionally equivalent under zero perturbation and establishes hyperparameter transfer enabling efficient tuning with reduced cost.

papers.title: $\texttt{MetaDistill}$: Unlocking the Performance Ceiling for Pretrained Optimizers
papers.contribution: MetaDistill significantly improves learnable optimizer generalization on BBOB test suite and control tasks compared to standard training paradigms.

papers.title: Adaptive Methods Are Preferable in High Privacy Settings: An SDE Perspective
papers.contribution: Shows adaptive methods dominate in high-privacy regimes with epsilon-independent optimal learning rates, making them far more practical.

papers.title: An Embarrassingly Simple Way to Optimize Orthogonal Matrices at Scale
papers.contribution: Optimizes problems with thousands of orthogonal matrices in minutes while alternatives take hours, setting milestone for exploiting orthogonality constraints at scale.

papers.title: Arbitrary-Order Block SignSGD for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: On Qwen3-8B, Llama3-8B, and Qwen3-32B converges faster per iteration with superior downstream performance while reducing runtime and memory compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Bi-LoRA: Efficient Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Fine-Tuning Large-Scale Models
papers.contribution: Bi-LoRA roughly halves SAM application time for LoRA while achieving both efficiency and effectiveness across diverse architectures and tasks.

papers.title: CALM Before the STORM: Unlocking Native Reasoning for Optimization Modeling
papers.contribution: We show that directly fine-tuning LRMs on already written-out Operations Research (OR) solutions can improve easier cases while hurting harder ones, suggesting that this training signal can interfere

papers.title: CALM: Co-evolution of Algorithms and Language Model for Automatic Heuristic Design
papers.contribution: CALM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on various optimization tasks using 7B INT4 quantized model on a single 24GB GPU.

papers.title: CONGA:Confidence-and-Gradient-Aware Learning Rate Schedule for Test Time Adaptation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that CONGA improves existing TTA methods as a plug-in with minimal overhead, validated through extensive experiments and theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Cautious Weight Decay
papers.contribution: Drop-in optimizer modification improving language model pre-training and ImageNet classification at million- to billion-parameter scales.

papers.title: Completed Hyperparameter Transfer across Modules, Width, Depth, Batch and Duration
papers.contribution: Demonstrates hyperparameter transfer holds per-layer and proposes simplified parameterization reducing search dimensionality without performance cost.

papers.title: Enabling Fine-Tuning of Direct Feedback Alignment via Feedback-Weight Matching
papers.contribution: Feedback-weight matching enables reliable DFA-based fine-tuning for the first time, achieving 7.97% accuracy improvement on image classification and 0.66 higher correlation on NLP tasks.

papers.title: Enhancing LLM Training via Spectral Clipping
papers.contribution: SPECTRA uniformly improves validation loss for various optimizers including AdamW, Signum, and Mars, with state-of-the-art results on LLM pretraining.

papers.title: Evolution Strategies at Scale: LLM Fine-Tuning Beyond Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: ES outperforms established RL implementations with improved tolerance to long-horizon rewards, robustness across base LLMs, reduced reward hacking, and better stability.

papers.title: Few-Shot Design Optimization by Exploiting Auxiliary Information
papers.contribution: Achieves improved few-shot prediction and faster design optimization on robotic hardware design and hyperparameter tuning, outperforming several multi-task optimization methods.

papers.title: Half-order Fine-Tuning for Diffusion Model: A Recursive Likelihood Ratio Optimizer
papers.contribution: RLR demonstrates theoretical convergence guarantees with superior image/video generation results; novel prompt technique achieves synergistic effects.

papers.title: HippoTune: A Hippocampal Associative Loop–Inspired Fine-Tuning Method for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: HippoTune outperforms classical buffer-free PEFT-CL methods by 5–8% in accuracy across vision benchmarks while reducing training FLOPs by 50%.

papers.title: Hyperparameter Transfer Laws for Non-Recurrent Multi-Path Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Unifies hyperparameter transfer across diverse non-recurrent architectures (CNNs, ResNets, Transformers) with a shared scaling law validated across experiments.

papers.title: IO-Adam: Rethinking Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimizers from Gradient Computation
papers.contribution: Reduces memory usage by up to 30% while preserving or improving performance compared to standard Adam.

papers.title: LOZO+: Provably Efficient Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning via Greedy Low-Rank Subspace Selection
papers.contribution: Theoretically proves LOZO+ converges faster than existing ZO methods while maintaining memory efficiency and achieving performance competitive with first-order methods.

papers.title: Landmark-Guided Policy Optimization for Multi-Objective Language Model Selection
papers.contribution: Reduces search time by average of 73% compared to exhaustive search while covering more than 99% of optimal target space hypervolume.

papers.title: One LR Doesn’t Fit All: Heavy-Tail Guided Layerwise Learning Rates for LLMs
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 1.5× training speedup, raising zero-shot accuracy from 47.09% to 49.02% for 1B models with low tuning overhead.

papers.title: Optimizer Choice Matters For The Emergence of Neural Collapse
papers.contribution: Proves NC cannot emerge under decoupled weight decay in adaptive optimizers like AdamW, establishes momentum's accelerating effect on NC with SGD across 3,900 training runs.

papers.title: Problem Distributions as Tasks: Repurposing Meta Learning for Generative Combinatorial Optimization towards Multi-task Pretraining and Adapt
papers.contribution: Achieves 9.16% performance gain with 95.6× inference acceleration; state-of-the-art on all test sets; 82% and 91% savings in training resources and time.

papers.title: Scaling Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization with Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Scales to ~1500 tasks without saturation; LLM initializations match or surpass from-scratch BO with far fewer oracle calls.

papers.title: Stabilizing Equation Learning via Zero-Point Constraints
papers.contribution: EQL-Z substantially improves exact equation recovery and in/out-of-distribution generalization over vanilla EQL, approaching leading symbolic regression baselines.

papers.title: Task-free Adaptive Meta Black-box Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive performance on synthetic benchmarks and UAV path planning without handcrafted training tasks.

papers.title: Theoretical Analysis of Sparse Optimization with Reparameterization, Weight Decay, and Adaptive Learning Rate
papers.contribution: ReWA leads to significant sparsity improvements over L1-regularization while preserving test accuracy on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet with ResNets.

papers.title: Thompson Sampling via Fine-Tuning of LLMs
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art sample and computational efficiency on FAQ refinement, protein search, and quantum circuit design, with a novel regret bound matching standard Thompson Sampling guarantees.

papers.title: Three Forward, One Backward: Memory-Efficient Full-Rank Fine-Tuning of Large Models via Extra Forward Passes
papers.contribution: LMAO achieves performance comparable to first-order methods with strict memory constraints and provides theoretical convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Towards Learned Optimization Free Lunch
papers.contribution: Scales to GPT-3 XL (1.3B parameters), six orders of magnitude larger than meta-training distribution, and generalizes across diverse out-of-distribution ML workloads.

papers.title: WSM: Decay-Free Learning Rate Schedule via Checkpoint Merging for LLM Pre-training
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms Warmup-Stable-Decay with improvements of +3.5% MATH, +2.9% HumanEval, +5.5% MMLU-Pro.

papers.title: Weight Decay Improves Language Model Plasticity
papers.contribution: Larger weight decay during pretraining increases downstream adaptability, leading to counterintuitive trade-offs where lower-performing base models adapt better after fine-tuning.

papers.title: Weight Decay may matter more than µP for Learning Rate Transfer in Practice
papers.contribution: Findings fundamentally challenge prevailing beliefs about learning rate transfer and explain why muP requires independent weight decay for effective transfer.
